idiom_name: hand-written row mapping over SQLite (GRDB FetchableRecord/PersistableRecord conformances)
implementation_notes: Swift's standard library has no persistence layer, and the platform frameworks are object-graph managers whose managed objects are persistence-aware (Core Data NSManagedObject, SwiftData @Model) - closer to Active Record than to a mapper. The Data Mapper structure is therefore hand-written: a plain struct plus decoding and encoding code that knows the columns. With GRDB that reduces to protocol conformances - Codable + FetchableRecord (or an explicit init(row:)) to load, PersistableRecord to insert/update - with DatabaseQueue/DatabasePool providing the connection and write blocks the transaction boundary. The struct keeps its invariants and never sees SQL.
pitfalls: Codable row decoding matches column names to property names exactly (case-sensitive); rename on the SQL side only with CodingKeys, or write an explicit init(row:).
Swift structs have value semantics, so there is no reference identity to lean on: an identity map needs explicit keying and Equatable/Hashable on a business key rather than all stored properties.
Database reads and writes are synchronous on the calling thread - run them off the main thread or wrap them, otherwise larger queries jank the UI.
Core Data/SwiftData managed objects are confined to their context and actor; passing them across contexts is a data race, and using them as the domain type re-couples the model to the framework.
